PRESIDENT STEVENS' LETTER ABOUT
THE CENTENNIAL
October 7, 1933
Dear Brothers in Psi Upsilon:
On November 24, 1833, seven young men, undergraduates in Union
CoUege at Schenectady, New York brought into existence the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity.
Fifty years later, our Fraternity celebrated its semi-centennial by a
great dinner in the home of its Founding, at which there were present
more than two hundred of its members, representing the seventeen Chap
ters which then constituted its Chapter Roll. Many of those who attended
that dinner nearly half a century ago are still alive and are looking forward
with keen enthusiasm to the even more important event in our Fraternity's
annals in which they hope to participate this fall.
The undergraduate Chapter delegates at the 1932 Convention of Psi
Upsilon, held vsdth the Delta Chapter of New York University a year
ago, voted unanimously to postpone the 1933 Convention until November
22 and 23, 1933, in order that it might merge into the Centennial Cele
bration of our Fraternity which will be held on November 24, 1933, at
Union CoUege where it was founded one hundred years before.
Plans have been completed for a fitting dedication on that date and
iu a prominent location on Union's Campus of a worthy Memorial to those
seven men, who, as undergraduates, founded our Fraternity on the broad
principle of friendship between frue young men of similar high standards
of thought and conduct, which has endured for a century.
A month after they founded Psi Upsilon, these same young men
drew that remarkable Constitution, whose Preamble and Initiation Ritual,
still practicaUy unchanged, have since thrilled generation after generation
of Psi U's. The old book, its pages still as clear and legible as ever, in
which these our Fraternity's fundamental ideals are recorded, with the
signatures of the Founders and scores of those who followed them, will
span the interval of a century and take back those of our number who
come to Psi Upsilon's Centennial to the college days of the first year of
the second term of Andrew Jackson's Presidency of the United States.
Furthermore, all present at the Centennial will have the privilege of
signing the origmal Constitution one hundred years after our founding,
and in another one hundred years it wiU again be signed by those who
foUow us.
